description.description: Line under the heading. Pass an empty string to hide it.

posts.description: Posts to list. Sorted newest first by date.

categories.description: Filter labels in order. "All" is added in front.

onCategoryChange.description: Called when a filter is picked. The page resets to 1.

onPageChange.description: Called from the page numbers and the previous and next buttons.

pageSize.description: Cards per page below the featured post.

showFeatured.description: Shows the post marked featured (or the newest) of the current filter as a large card on page one.

getHref.description: Link for each post. When set, cards are plain links and the in-place reader is off.

onPostOpen.description: Called when a post opens, for analytics or routing.

posts.title: The case for quiet software
posts.excerpt: Why we removed half the colors from our interface and people started finishing work faster.

image.alt: A bright living room with timber beams, arched windows, and cream sofas

body: Last spring we ran an experiment. We took the busiest screen in the product and removed every color that did not carry meaning. Status stayed. Selection stayed. Everything else went neutral.
Nobody asked for it, and almost nobody noticed the change directly. What they noticed was that the screen felt easier. Task completion went up eleven percent in the first month.
Quiet does not mean empty. It means every element has a job, and the loud moments are saved for the things that need attention.

posts.title: How offline sync actually works
posts.excerpt: Conflict free replicated data, explained with the bugs we hit on the way to shipping it.

image.alt: A white tiled building facade with curved balconies

body: Every edit you make is stored locally first and sent to the server when a connection is available. The hard part is what happens when two people change the same thing while apart.
We use a sequence CRDT for text and last writer wins for simple fields, with a few careful exceptions we cover here.

posts.title: What we learned from a week in Lisbon
posts.excerpt: Forty people, one shared roadmap, and no slides allowed. Notes from our autumn offsite.

image.alt: Terracotta rooftops of Lisbon running down to the river

body: We banned slides for the week. Every session started with a written memo and ten minutes of silent reading.
It was the most productive offsite we have run, and the roadmap we left with has held up better than any before it.

posts.title: Shared views are here
posts.excerpt: Save a filter, name it, and share it with your team. Everyone sees the same thing, always current.

image.alt: A home office with a wooden desk and deep green walls

body: Saved filters were the most requested feature of the year. Today they become shared views: name a view, pick who sees it, and it stays in sync as the data changes.

posts.title: Choosing a type scale you will not regret
posts.excerpt: Seven sizes, two weights, and the rules we use to keep them that way as the product grows.

image.alt: Curved stainless steel panels of the Walt Disney Concert Hall against a blue sky

body: A type scale is a promise. Every new size you add makes the next decision harder.
We settled on seven sizes and two weights, and wrote down when each one is allowed.

posts.title: Making search ten times faster
posts.excerpt: A new query planner, a smarter index, and one very embarrassing N plus one we found along the way.

image.alt: Layered mountain ridges under a warm evening sky

body: Search used to take around 400 milliseconds at the ninety fifth percentile. It now takes 38.
Most of the gain came from the planner. The rest came from deleting code we should never have written.

posts.title: The rituals that keep a remote team close
posts.excerpt: Written standups, demo Fridays and the one meeting we will never cancel.

image.alt: A sunroom with a round dining table, plants, and windows on three sides

body: We work across nine time zones. The rituals that survive are the ones that respect that.

posts.title: Usage insights for every workspace
posts.excerpt: See which features your team relies on, where people get stuck, and what changed this week.

image.alt: A calm alpine lake reflecting a rocky peak at golden hour

body: Admins can now open Insights from workspace settings. It shows adoption per feature, trends over time and a weekly summary by email.

posts.title: Motion should explain, not decorate
posts.excerpt: Our rules for animation: every movement answers where something came from or where it went.

image.alt: Wavy terracotta walls rising toward a blue sky

body: If you cannot say what an animation explains, remove it. That single rule removed a third of our motion code.

posts.title: Upgrading Postgres with zero downtime
posts.excerpt: Logical replication, a dry run on a copy of production, and a cutover that took four seconds.

image.alt: A long coastline with waves rolling onto a beach below green cliffs

body: We moved two terabytes to a new major version while customers kept working. Here is the runbook.

posts.title: Our next chapter
posts.excerpt: We raised a Series B to build the calmest tool for teams. Here is what changes and what does not.

image.alt: A calm sea at dusk with a low island on the horizon

body: The product stays the same price. The team doubles. The roadmap gets faster.

posts.title: A keyboard shortcut for everything
posts.excerpt: Press question mark anywhere to see every shortcut, then make your own.

image.alt: A grey armchair and ottoman with a knit throw in a dark green room

body: Every action in the product now has a shortcut, and you can remap any of them from settings.

posts.title: Naming color tokens by job, not by hue
posts.excerpt: Why surface and border beat gray-100 and gray-200, and how we migrated four hundred files.

image.alt: A modern glass house beside a long pool under a clear sky

body: Semantic tokens let dark mode, high contrast and brand themes share one component codebase.
